topics.title: Distributed systems glossary: terms we keep mistranslating
topics.body:
idempotent — an operation that produces the same result whether applied once or many times. In HTTP: PUT and DELETE are idempotent, POST is not.

eventual consistency — replicas may diverge temporarily but converge given no new writes. Always state the convergence window; "eventually" without a bound is not a specification.

backpressure — a mechanism that lets a slow consumer signal a fast producer to slow down. Without it, an unbounded queue converts a latency problem into an out-of-memory problem.

Note: "幂等" is frequently mistranslated as "idempotence" in noun position when the sentence needs the adjective "idempotent". Prefer the adjective: "an idempotent endpoint", not "an endpoint with idempotence".
